title: Big and small
subtopics: Big and small objects in the classroom
Big and small in my family and compound
Finding the big one and the small one
objectives: Children will point to the big or the small one when asked.
Children will say or sign big and small with support.
content: Comparing two objects by size and using the words big and small in play, songs and routines.
teachingActivities: Model big and small with exaggerated voice and gesture; hold up two objects and ask "Where is the big one?"; narrate children’s actions with the words.
learnerActivities: Handle, carry and roll big and small objects; point, show and say big or small; match big and small in a basket game.
resources: Big and small plastic cups and bowls
Big and small drums or tins
assessment: Observe whether each child chooses the big or small object on request; record on the class record sheet.
expectedOutcomes: Chooses the big or small object on request in most turns.
Uses the words big and small with prompting.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: tidying away in two baskets

lessons.title: Daddy’s sandal, baby’s sandal
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Big and small objects in the classroom
objectives: Children will point to the big sandal or the small sandal when asked.
successCriteria: Points to the big sandal on request
Looks at both sandals before choosing
lessons.previousKnowledge: No prior mathematics is needed. Children have seen big and small things at home, for example an adult’s sandal and a baby’s sandal.
resources: One adult sandal and one child sandal
Two puppets or soft toys (one large, one small)
lessons.starter: Sit the children in a half circle on a mat. Put on the adult sandal and say in a big, slow voice, "This is a big sandal. Big!" Then hold up the small sandal and whisper, "This is a small sandal. Small!"
teacherActivities: Place the adult sandal and the child sandal side by side on the mat. Point to each and say "big" in a deep voice and "small" in a tiny voice, three times.
Ask "Where is the big sandal?" and wait. Gently guide a hand if a child is unsure.
Ask "Where is the small sandal?" Swap the positions of the sandals and ask again.
Bring in the two puppets. Say "Big puppet wears the big sandal. Small puppet wears the small sandal." Let each child try putting a sandal on the correct puppet.
learnerActivities: Children copy the voices and gestures: arms wide for big, fingers close together for small.
Each child takes a turn to touch the big sandal.
Children touch the small sandal and say or whisper "small".
Children put the sandal on the correct puppet and show the puppet to a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Place the adult sandal and the child sandal side by side on the mat. Point to each and say "big" in a deep voice and "small" in a tiny voice, three times. Children: Children copy the voices and gestures: arms wide for big, fingers close together for small.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Where is the big sandal?" and wait. Gently guide a hand if a child is unsure. Children: Each child takes a turn to touch the big sandal.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Where is the small sandal?" Swap the positions of the sandals and ask again. Children: Children touch the small sandal and say or whisper "small".

Step 4. Teacher: Bring in the two puppets. Say "Big puppet wears the big sandal. Small puppet wears the small sandal." Let each child try putting a sandal on the correct puppet. Children: Children put the sandal on the correct puppet and show the puppet to a friend.

practical.title: Sandal parade
steps: Line up the children’s own sandals with an adult’s sandal on the mat.
Ask each child, one at a time, to find "your small sandal" and then "the big sandal".
Children carry their small sandal to the shelf and the big one to the teacher.
practical.safety: Check the floor is dry and clear. Children sit while handling sandals; no walking while wearing adult sandals.

differentiation.support: Offer only two items with a very obvious size difference and use a hand-over-hand point. Say the word for the child and wait for any sign or sound in reply.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another big thing and another small thing in the room and bring them to the mat.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Show me the big sandal.
questions.expected: Child points to or touches the adult sandal.

questions.question: Which one is small?
questions.expected: Child points to the child sandal and may say "small".

expectedOutcomes: Chooses the big sandal in most turns
Says or signs big or small with prompting
lessons.conclusion: Hold up the two sandals one last time. Clap and say "Big! Small!" together. Children put the sandals back in two places: big on the left, small on the right.
lessons.homeConnection: At home, find a grown-up’s shoe and a child’s shoe. Say "big" and "small" while you point, then ask your child to find the small one.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "point to the big sandal or the small sandal when asked" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Rolling big and small balls
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Big and small objects in the classroom
objectives: Children will push and roll a big ball and a small ball and say which is big and which is small with support.
successCriteria: Points to the big ball when asked
lessons.previousKnowledge: No prior mathematics is needed. Children have seen big and small things at home, for example an adult’s sandal and a baby’s sandal.
resources: One big soft ball and one small soft ball
Two baskets, one large and one small
lessons.starter: Roll the big ball slowly across the floor to a child and say "Here comes the big ball!" Then roll the small ball and say "Here comes the small ball!" Let each child feel them.
teacherActivities: Sit in a circle. Roll the big ball to a child, say "big ball", and ask them to roll it back.
Repeat with the small ball and say "small ball".
Show the two baskets. Say "Big basket for the big ball. Small basket for the small ball."
Mix the balls and ask "Can you find the big ball?" while pointing to neither.
learnerActivities: Child rolls the big ball back; the group says "big" as it travels.
Children roll the small ball and say or whisper "small".
Children take turns to put each ball in the matching basket.
Children point to and pick up the big ball.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sit in a circle. Roll the big ball to a child, say "big ball", and ask them to roll it back. Children: Child rolls the big ball back; the group says "big" as it travels.
Step 2. Teacher: Repeat with the small ball and say "small ball". Children: Children roll the small ball and say or whisper "small".
Step 3. Teacher: Show the two baskets. Say "Big basket for the big ball. Small basket for the small ball." Children: Children take turns to put each ball in the matching basket.
Step 4. Teacher: Mix the balls and ask "Can you find the big ball?" while pointing to neither. Children: Children point to and pick up the big ball.

practical.title: Ball and basket game
steps: Spread two big and two small soft balls on the floor.
Say "Find a big ball." Child brings it to the big basket.
Say "Find a small ball." Child brings it to the small basket.
practical.safety: Use soft balls larger than a child’s fist. Keep the floor clear and the group seated except when it is a child’s turn.

differentiation.support: Use only one ball at a time and say the size word as the ball is placed in the basket.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a bigger ball than the small one by choosing from three sizes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which ball goes in the big basket?
Can you show me the small ball?
questions.expected: Child holds up or points to the small ball.

expectedOutcomes: Matches big ball to big basket
lessons.conclusion: Sing the "Big, small" rhyme from Day 1 while rolling the balls one more time. Tidy up by placing the big ball and small ball in their baskets together.
lessons.homeConnection: Use a small orange and a big orange, or a big and a small spoon, and ask your child to give you the big one.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "push and roll a big ball and a small ball and say which is big and which is small with support" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Find the big cup, find the small cup
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Finding the big one and the small one
objectives: Children will choose the big or small cup when asked and say the word with support.
successCriteria: Chooses the correct cup in at least two of three turns
Says or signs one size word
lessons.previousKnowledge: No prior mathematics is needed. Children have seen big and small things at home, for example an adult’s sandal and a baby’s sandal.
resources: Four plastic cups: two big, two small
A bucket of water and a sponge for the outdoor extension (optional)
lessons.starter: Hold up a big cup and a small cup and say "I am thirsty! Which cup holds more water? The big cup!" Pretend to drink from each cup and let children join in.
teacherActivities: Put the big and small cup on the tray. Ask "Show me the big cup."
Ask "Now show me the small cup." Swap places and ask again.
Hold the cups behind your back and ask "Which hand has the big cup?" Reveal slowly.
Give each pair of children a tray with a big and small cup. Say "Give your friend the small cup."
learnerActivities: Child points to or lifts the big cup.
Child points to the small cup and says "small" if able.
Children point to the hand and shout "big!" or "small!".
Child gives the small cup to a friend and says "small" or "for you".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the big and small cup on the tray. Ask "Show me the big cup." Children: Child points to or lifts the big cup.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Now show me the small cup." Swap places and ask again. Children: Child points to the small cup and says "small" if able.
Step 3. Teacher: Hold the cups behind your back and ask "Which hand has the big cup?" Reveal slowly. Children: Children point to the hand and shout "big!" or "small!".
Step 4. Teacher: Give each pair of children a tray with a big and small cup. Say "Give your friend the small cup." Children: Child gives the small cup to a friend and says "small" or "for you".

practical.title: Cup trays
steps: Each child receives a tray with two cups.
Teacher calls "big" or "small" and children lift that cup.
Swap trays with a friend and play again.
practical.safety: Use unbreakable plastic cups with no sharp edges and no water inside indoors; supervise at all times.

differentiation.support: Offer one very big and one very small cup and place them far apart.
differentiation.extension: Introduce a third, middle-sized cup and ask "Which is the biggest?" with gestures.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Show me the small cup.
questions.expected: Child lifts or points to the small cup.

questions.question: Is this cup big or small?
questions.expected: Child says or shows the correct word.

expectedOutcomes: Finds the big or small cup on request
Gives the small cup to a friend
lessons.conclusion: Stack the cups together, big at the bottom, small on the top. Say "Big goes first!" and tidy them into the basket together.
lessons.homeConnection: At mealtime, ask your child to pass you the big cup or the small plate and name it together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "choose the big or small cup when asked and say the word with support" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The big yam and the small yam
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Big and small in my family and compound
objectives: Children will use the words big and small while listening to a story and acting it out.
successCriteria: Joins in saying big or small at the right moment
Acts big or small with their body
lessons.previousKnowledge: No prior mathematics is needed. Children have seen big and small things at home, for example an adult’s sandal and a baby’s sandal.
resources: A story picture of a big yam and a small yam (or two toy yams, or a big and small cassava)
lessons.starter: Walk in carrying a basket on your head with a big yam in it. Say "Mama went to the market!" in a storytelling voice and let the children guess what is in the basket.
teacherActivities: Tell the story slowly, holding up the big yam on "big" and the small yam on "small". Pause before each word and look at the children.
Tell it again and invite children to be the big yam (stretch up) or the small yam (curl small) when they hear the word.
Place the big yam and small yam on the mat and ask "Which one fits in baby’s bag?"
learnerActivities: Children say "big" or "small" when you pause and show it with their arms or fingers.
Children stretch tall or curl down according to the word.
Children point to the small yam and say or whisper "small".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the story slowly, holding up the big yam on "big" and the small yam on "small". Pause before each word and look at the children. Children: Children say "big" or "small" when you pause and show it with their arms or fingers.

Step 2. Teacher: Tell it again and invite children to be the big yam (stretch up) or the small yam (curl small) when they hear the word. Children: Children stretch tall or curl down according to the word.
Step 3. Teacher: Place the big yam and small yam on the mat and ask "Which one fits in baby’s bag?" Children: Children point to the small yam and say or whisper "small".

practical.title: Be the yam
steps: Play the drum slowly for big and fast for small.
Children walk with big steps for slow drum beats and tiny steps for fast beats.
Stop and call "big!" or "small!" for children to freeze in that shape.
practical.safety: Space children well apart and walk, never run. Use toy or large real yams that cannot be swallowed and keep them off the floor.

differentiation.support: Pair the child with an adult for each movement and use an exaggerated gesture.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find something big and something small at home to tell the class on Monday.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which yam was too big for the bag?

expectedOutcomes: Uses big and small words in a story
Moves in a big or small way on request
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the yams. Say together, "Big yam, small yam. Goodbye!" Children carry the pretend yams to the basket.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell your child the yam story at bath time. Use real vegetables, such as a big and a small tomato.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use the words big and small while listening to a story and acting it out" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A woman at a market with a big yam
A baby and a small yam
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Big yam, big yam, stretch up high. Small yam, small yam, curl up small.
learnerFacing.story: Mama went to the market. She bought a big yam. Big, big, big! The yam was too big for her bag, so she carried it on her head. Then she bought a small yam. Small, small, small! The small yam fitted into her bag. At home she cooked the big yam for the family and the small yam for baby. Everyone clapped. Big and small, big and small.

lessons.title: Big and small stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Finding the big one and the small one
objectives: Children will choose the big or small object at three play stations.
successCriteria: Says or signs a size word at least once
lessons.previousKnowledge: No prior mathematics is needed. Children have seen big and small things at home, for example an adult’s sandal and a baby’s sandal.
resources: Station 2: big and small balls and baskets
lessons.starter: Show the three stations and sing the "Big, small" rhyme while pointing to each. Tell the children that today they will play at each station with a friend.
teacherActivities: Rotate children in groups of three or four through the three stations every four minutes. Say the size word only if the child is stuck.
At each station ask "Where is the big one?" and "Where is the small one?" and watch how each child responds.
Photograph or note one example of each child’s work for the class record.
learnerActivities: Children play and choose big or small objects at each station.
Children show or say their answers.
Children continue playing and tidy their station when the signal sounds.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate children in groups of three or four through the three stations every four minutes. Say the size word only if the child is stuck. Children: Children play and choose big or small objects at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Where is the big one?" and "Where is the small one?" and watch how each child responds. Children: Children show or say their answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Photograph or note one example of each child’s work for the class record. Children: Children continue playing and tidy their station when the signal sounds.

practical.title: Station circuit
steps: Teacher stays at one station for observation, a helper rotates the others.
Children move on when the shaker rings.
At the end each child chooses a favourite station to visit again.
practical.safety: Keep walkways clear, supervise each station and use only large, soft items. Ensure children sit while handling objects.

differentiation.support: Keep a child at one station with an adult for the whole time if a transition is difficult.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to be the "station leader" and ask a friend "Where is the big one?".

assessment.method: Observe each child at the three stations. Record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: chooses big or small on request; uses the words big and small.

questions.question: Where is the big one?
questions.expected: Child points to the larger object.

questions.question: Can you find the small ball?
questions.expected: Child picks up or points to the small ball.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
Chooses big or small independently in most turns
lessons.conclusion: Gather the children and sing the "Big, small" rhyme one last time. Let each child hold up one big and one small object as the class lines up.
lessons.homeConnection: Send home a note: "This week we learned big and small. Please point out one big and one small thing each day."
teacherReflection: Which children could show "choose the big or small object at three play stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
